name: The Mount, Edith Wharton’s Home
source: The Mount’s website and media library; OpenStreetMap
note: The Mount is the house Edith Wharton designed and built in 1902, where she wrote The House of Mirth. It has no art collection to speak of: what you see are the rooms she planned by the rules of The Decoration of Houses, her own 2,700-book library, and the gardens she called better than her novels. This guide lists every room on the house tour, the books The Mount shows from her library, the gardens, the Stable, NightWood and the 2026 outdoor sculpture show (ended October 24). The house is open weekends only from November to January 2, then closed until May; the grounds are free all year.
